# harfbuzz

[harfbuzz/harfbuzz](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/harfbuzz](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/harfbuzz)

**Status: available.** 3 of OSS-Fuzz's 6 fuzz targets have statements. 12 binaries, 30 MB. 31 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 31 open.

Built from harfbuzz (commit `cf30f712`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [hb-repacker-fuzzer](hb-repacker-fuzzer/) | Decodes a table tag, an object list (blobs) and a link list from the input into hb_subset_serialize_object_t graph nodes and calls hb_subset_serialize_or_fail (the repacker); the packed blob is destroyed unread, so the repacker's output is never checked for overflow-freedom or for preserving the graph. | none | 15 |
| [hb-shape-fuzzer](hb-shape-fuzzer/) | Loads the fuzzed font, shapes a fixed ASCII string and then a 16-codepoint UTF-32 string derived from the input (plus test_font() from test/api/test-ot-face.c, which calls most hb_ot_* / hb_font_* getters and discards the results). | none | 7 |
| [hb-subset-fuzzer](hb-subset-fuzzer/) | Loads the fuzzed font and runs hb_subset_or_fail with a fixed codepoint set, then (legacy mode) with codepoints/flags/pinned axis locations read from the input tail, or (extended "HBSUBFZ2" mode) with an op stream editing flags, sets, text and axis ranges. hb_face_collect_unicodes is also called. | 1 check (invariant; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9 |

Not included: **api-driver** (held from this release); **hb-gpu-fuzzer** (built, but not included in this release yet); **hb-raster-fuzzer** (built, but not included in this release yet); **hb-vector-fuzzer** (built, but not included in this release yet).

## What the statements say, for harfbuzz
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch harfbuzz
    ./oft verify-sha harfbuzz

By hand: download `harfbuzz-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/harfbuzz/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [harfbuzz/harfbuzz](https://github.com/harfbuzz/harfbuzz) at `cf30f712e73937b3954c57d9521e2e021671527c`, built with CMake
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
